checks.tolerance: Hides source object key 622 (folder), exports the original scene and reimports it: the folder reads back hidden and the character inside it stays visible. The CharaStudio side of ST-T03 visibility (reloading the exported scene in the original player) is not covered here.

Renames source object key 622 (folder), exports the original scene and reimports it: the new name reads back. Camera and route renames are not exercised because the fixture scene contains neither object type; the character-name rejection half of ST-T03 rename is a StudioModel export guard covered by the Engine suite.

Edits face slot 20 on character key 0 and body slot 0 on character key 65, exports the original scene and reimports it: both rates read back within 1e-5. The inspector's live visual update and Reset to card are not covered (no headless pixel or reset assertion).

Edits the body.skinMainColor card color on character key 0, exports the original scene and reimports it: the edited rgba reads back on every component within 1e-5. The hair color edit is NOT part of this scenario: hair.parts.0.baseColor is a draft color on this card but binds no material on the imported assembly, so export skips the writeback; the live preview update and Reset to card stay unchecked.

Selects catalog clip [0,2,0] on character key 0 (saved clip [0,4,0]) with speed 1.5 and forceLoop on: the live animation state the preview plays matches the group/category/no exactly, speed within 1e-5, loop equal; after the original-scene export and reimport the new catalog IDs, speed and loop read back unchanged, and control character key 65 still reports its saved clip [0,0,2]. The clip actually plays on screen is not asserted (no pixel check).

Rotates FK bone 19 of character key 65 to [0,35,0] degrees (which also turns FK on): the document holds the exact degrees within 1e-5 and the left-hand guide (bone 21) sits further than 1e-5 from its pre-edit position. After export and reimport the guide lands within 0.02 of its post-edit position: export writes the degrees into the character's bone record, so after reimport the pose is asserted by bone position, not by the document's edit overlay (import never repopulates that overlay). IK mode and IK target edits stay unchecked.

Drives the REAL mouse handlers (mouseDown / eight mouseDragged / mouseUp, left button, no modifiers) over the GPU pick pass: the scenario projects bone 19's guide origin with the view camera, scans ±120 px for a pixel whose pick id is the z rotate ring (the z ring is the one open to this scene's view camera; y and x project nearly edge-on there), grabs it and drags 60,40 px. The drag must hold a non-zero FK rotation on bone 19 (the angle comes out of the ring geometry, so it is asserted non-zero, not equal to a number) and move the left-hand guide (bone 21) further than 1e-5 from its pre-drag position. Exactly one undo snapshot is pushed (by mouseDown), so one undo restores the hand within 1e-4; after redo, export and reimport the guide lands within 0.02 of its post-drag position. The drag degree readback and picked pixel id are recorded in the step detail. Before the drag, a hoverGizmo step drives the REAL mouseMoved hover (R7 phase 2, item 5), which picks asynchronously for the latest mouse position only: over the same z ring and an off-gizmo corner of the scan box, in three sequences of moves partly faster than a pick completes, each settled the way a click settles the hover first. on-off-on must highlight the z ring, off and on-off nothing (the ring's result arrives stale and is dropped); after each, the hovered axis must equal what the synchronous pick finds at the final position, and the frame the app built must draw exactly that ring (or no axis) in the highlight color. The six moves must coalesce three times, apply three results and drop at least two stale ones.

With IKKOKU_STUDIO_ITEM_CATALOG set, the import diagnostics must report `Items rendered from the converted catalog: 19; unmapped keys: none.`, and an export of all 19 placeholder items plus a reimport must still report that line. The rendered transforms and saved colors of the props (the visual half of ST-T04) are not asserted.

On scene-x (two active cameras, IKKOKU-A key 0 and IKKOKU-B key 2) the import must pick the last active camera in depth-first order (key 2) as the load winner; toggling camera 0 must make it active, and after export+reimport the written flags must make key 0 the winner again. This exercises our own load/export rule (ST-A06/ST-T03 active camera); reloading the exported scene in the original CharaStudio player is not covered.

On scene-x, toggling the active camera key 2 off must leave no active camera (orbit view); export writes every camera flag false and a reimport must still show no active camera. Deactivating key 0 (not the winner) is not scripted; the reload happens in our importer, not the original player.

Renames camera object key 0 on scene-x, exports the original scene and reimports it: the new name reads back on the camera placeholder (the camera-object half of ST-T03 rename, which the folder-only rename-folder scenario could not reach). The active-camera flags stay untouched by the rename; the winner (key 2) is not re-asserted here.

On the stt11c route scene (routes key 0 and key 3, both saved active) the inspector must report key 0 playing; toggling it must stop it, and after export+reimport key 0 must read back stopped (its flag written) while key 3 still reads back playing (its flag untouched). Only the play-state flag round trip is asserted; whether the character actually animates along the route is not observable headlessly.

ST-T11 route children: on the CharaStudio-authored scene-route-children.png (route key 0, saved playing and looping over four points; its children are folder key 9 and the fixture female key 10, which renders on the route) both children's world positions, read through the same placement walk refresh() renders with, move more than 0.5 m in a 2 s advance and the folder more than 0.1 m in the next 0.5 s; stopping the route pins both back to point 0 (within 1e-5 of their start) and they hold there through a further 2 s advance, and after export+reimport the route reads back stopped and both children still hold. Speed parity with the original tween, the Play all / Replay all / Stop all buttons and rendered pixels are not asserted.

ST-T11/ST-T03 route edits on the stt11c route scene (routes key 0 and key 3, both saved playing), every edit through the app's own StudioModel calls: a point drag through the guide's x arrow (mouse down/drag/up on the projected handle and arrow pixels) moves point 2 of the playing route; adding a point and deleting the start point are refused, and so are an ease outside CharaStudio's six-entry list and a speed edit on a curve point linked to the curve before it; after Stop, Add point appends point 4 at the last point with speed 2, linear ease and the uninitialised (1, 1, 1) aid; speed, ease, curve connection (InitAidPos places the aid halfway to the next point), link, loop, orientation, colour and line edits read back from the route state; undo/redo flips the line setting and the drawn line batches (2 to 1); route 3's aid drag and start-point rotation drag apply, and deleting its point 3 stops that route. Export then reimport reads both routes back unedited with every captured point and setting, the added point and aid as keys 18/19 (the smallest free keys), key 0 playing, key 3 stopped and renamed, one drawn line; a negative control rejects comparing route 3 with route 0's capture. The CharaStudio reload of the same export is Tools/reverse/original_scene_reload_probe.py (route-edit label).

ST-T11/ST-T03 route copies on the CharaStudio-authored scene-route-children.png (route key 0 playing, children folder 9 and the fixture female 10): a guide drag and a point move with undo/redo, then Stop and Play (a move under a playing route changes only the segments that start later, so the replay makes the 1.5 s captures a fresh Play of the moved points), then Duplicate of the route copies it with its children and points; the copy's settings are locked while it plays, and after Stop its curve and point moves apply and it plays again. After a 1.5 s advance the copy's folder is not where the original's is (negative control); a native save and in-process load keep both routes' edits, and after another 1.5 s advance each child is within 1e-3 m and 0.1 degrees of its pre-save capture. Export then reimport reads the original route's keys back unchanged and the copy as route 157 with point keys 306/308/310/312 and aid keys 307-313 (after its children 158 and 159), and the children land within 1e-3 m and 0.1 degrees of their captures after 1.5 s. The CharaStudio reload of the same export is Tools/reverse/original_scene_reload_probe.py (route-children-edit label).

The reload half of the route-children-edit save: a fresh process loads the saved document with no import; both route runtimes rehydrate once, route 0 plays from its saved flag and keeps its edited point 1, the copy keeps its moved points and its curve point 3 (a negative control rejects the original's point 1 on the copy), and both routes' folders move during a 1.5 s advance. ST-T11/ST-T01.

ST-T11 point moves under a playing route on scene-route-children.png, by CharaStudio's queue rule (StudioTween reads a segment's point transforms when that segment starts): route 0 and its Duplicate copy are played again at the same instant and their folders 9 agree within 1e-5 m and 0.1 degrees 0.9 s in; moving route 0's point 1 (the target of the segment in progress) and, 0.6 s later, a guide drag of its point 2 leave route 0's folder within 1e-5 m and 0.1 degrees of the unedited copy's (no jump, the segment in progress keeps its targets), and 1.0 s later, in the next segment, the folders are more than 0.05 m apart (negative control: the later segment takes the moved points). A drag control rejects the pre-drag route capture at point 2.

R4/ST-A06 mirrored camera parent: on the CharaStudio-authored scene-mirrored-camera.png (camera IKKOKU-MIRROR key 2 under item key 0 with scale (-1, 1, 1), saved active; control camera IKKOKU-CONTROL key 3 under item key 1 with scale (1, 1, 1)) the load winner is camera 2, and through StudioModel.viewCamera the preview renders from exactly the saved scene camera while the status line reports 'Source camera "IKKOKU-MIRROR" (camera 2) view unresolved: Source camera object parent frame is mirrored' and the view indicator reads 'Saved camera shown: source camera "IKKOKU-MIRROR" (camera 2) has a mirrored parent', never 'Viewing through'; the tree labels read 'IKKOKU-MIRROR (camera 2)' and 'IKKOKU-CONTROL (camera 3)'; toggling camera 3 looks through it with the indicator 'Viewing through source camera "IKKOKU-CONTROL" (camera 3)' (view position within 1e-5 of its world placement and forward within 0.01 degrees, not the saved camera), toggling camera 2 back falls back again, and after export+reimport the same holds; deactivating camera 3 last leaves no active camera, the saved view, an empty indicator and the status 'Source camera "IKKOKU-CONTROL" (camera 3) deactivated; orbit controls restored.' On the stt11c route scene, stopping route key 0 and renaming key 3 then undoing must keep both route runtimes live (2 entries; before ST-T15 the undo dropped them), roll the key 3 name back, and keep the runtime play state: key 0 stays stopped because play state is runtime-only and never part of an undo snapshot. Saves the imported props scene natively (StudioModel.saveScene, a Studio document card under .local/) after hiding folder key 622; the 19 converted item entries and the scene light must still be live after the save (saving must not disturb the runtime), and the hidden folder must read back hidden. Loads the document the previous check saved, in a fresh process with NO IKKOKU_SOURCE_SCENE (the import never runs; the scenario's first step is loadDocument): folder key 622 must read back hidden and the 19 converted item entries and the scene light must be rehydrated from the original scene file the card names. Saves scene-x natively with the load-winner camera (key 2) live: both camera cache entries and the scene light must survive the save untouched. The reload half is the next, ordered check. ST-T01.

Loads the saved scene-x card in a fresh process with no import: both camera entries and the scene light must be rehydrated and the look-through camera must be key 2, the FILE's load winner — the live camera choice a user had before the save is runtime state the document never carried and deliberately does not come back. ST-T01.

Stops route key 0 on the stt11c route scene, then saves the document natively: both route entries and the scene light must survive, and the live play state must still report key 0 stopped (the save must not rewrite play state through the caches). The reload half is the next, ordered check. ST-T01.

Loads the saved route card in a fresh process with no import: both route runtimes and the scene light must be rehydrated and key 0 must report playing again, because play state restarts from the SAVED flag (true; the live stop before the save was runtime-only, exactly as after an undo keeps it). Whether the character animates along the route is not observable headlessly. ST-T01.

Character 65's TARGET eye look is live against the lane scene's camera; dragging the view left and right flips both iris-shift angle rates between the saturated (+1, +1) and (-1, -1) sides, raising and lowering it moves the vertical rate past +/-0.5, and the head and neck bone positions stay exactly still (no eye bones exist, so the eyes never move the skeleton). Character 65's neck carries the FIX override ("FIX holds the saved neck rotation."): orbiting the camera across the scene never moves its head or neck bone. No TARGET/AWAY neck character exists in any scene under the fixture root, so the animated-neck half of ST-T07 neck look stays unautomated.

ST-T07 neck look TARGET/AWAY: on the CharaStudio-authored scene-neck-target.png, character 0 (neck pattern 1, TARGET) and character 147 (neck pattern 2, AWAY), both eyes pattern 1 (TARGET), get the live gaze runtime. The turn is measured on the front-hair root bone 100 (cf_J_hairF_00, a head child; a pure neck/head yaw leaves the head bone's own position unmoved) in each character's rig frame: orbiting the camera 60 degrees to one side moves the TARGET hair more than 0.05 and the AWAY hair more than 0.15, and the two end more than 0.15 apart (opposite sides); orbiting to the other side moves the TARGET hair more than 0.1 again while the AWAY hair returns within 0.01 of its front-camera pose and is again more than 0.15 from TARGET's. After export+reimport the gaze is live again and both poses reproduce within 0.01. Exact turn angles against the original are recorded in docs, not asserted; the FK-neck half of ST-T07 neck look stays unautomated.

Without a converted pattern library the saved [5, 6] pair is reported ("the pattern is never guessed") and both captured hand bones hold their incoming pose across a live 0.0667 s step; the pair survives export and reimport.

R7 phase 2, item 3: on the 7-character scenario scene, each editDuringAdvance step starts the live step the way the timer does (off the main thread; a serial step fails the op), lands an edit through the app's own method while the step is in flight (none, move key 65 by 0.25 m in x, FK bone 19 of key 65 to [0,35,0], undo, redo), then completes the step as its completion handler does. Each must advance the clock by exactly one 1/30 s step, present a 512x512 render byte-identical to a full main-thread rebuild of the same document at the same clock, and reuse exactly the step frames the contract allows: all of them without an edit, all but the moved character's after the document-only move, none after an edit that reached a preview (FK, undo, redo). The fk asserts read the edited document; after export and reimport only the character's presence is asserted, since the round trip is not what this check covers.
